papers.title: Robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty: does improved precision translate into better clinical outcomes? A systematic review
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty (R-THA) is being adopted progressively because of its potential to improve implant positioning and restore hip biomechanics more accurately than conventional techniques. However, whether these technical advantages translate into meaningful clinical benefits remains uncertain. This systematic review compared robot-assisted and conventional THA regarding implant positioning, restoration of hip biomechanics, functional outcomes, and complications. Materials and methods A systematic review was performed according to the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed and Scopus were searched for comparative studies published between 2015 and September 2025 evaluating robot-assisted versus conventional THA. After applying predefined eligibility criteria, 13 studies were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the MINORS and RoB 2 tools, and findings were synthesized qualitatively. Results Robot-assisted THA was consistently associated with greater accuracy of acetabular component placement within established safe zones and more precise restoration of limb length. Functional outcomes were inconsistent across studies, with no clear evidence of superior patient-reported outcomes or overall clinical benefit. Several studies reported lower rates of dislocation and reoperation following robot-assisted THA, although differences in overall complication rates were less consistent. Conclusions Robot-assisted THA improves the accuracy of implant positioning and better reproduces the preoperative surgical plan than conventional THA. However, these technical advantages have not translated into superior functional outcomes in the short to medium term. Longer-term studies are needed to determine their impact on implant survival.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文为机器人辅助全髋关节置换的临床系统综述，不涉及股骨柄应力遮挡、微动或有限元建模，与髋植入物生物力学方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This is a clinical systematic review of robot-assisted THA outcomes; it contains no finite element modeling, no proximal femur stress/strain or Gruen zone analysis, no micromotion or contact/friction modeling, and no implant design or boundary condition data.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估机器人辅助全髋置换的技术精度能否转化为临床获益。
summary_zh.method: 按PRISMA系统检索2015-2025年比较研究，纳入13篇并定性综合。
summary_zh.result: 髋臼假体定位更准、肢体长度恢复更好，但功能结局无一致优势。
summary_zh.validation: 基于临床文献的系统综述与偏倚风险评估。

summary_en.motivation: To determine whether the improved technical precision of robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty translates into measurable clinical benefits over conventional techniques.
summary_en.method: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of comparative studies published between 2015 and September 2025, with 13 studies assessed using MINORS and RoB 2 and synthesized qualitatively.
summary_en.result: Robot-assisted THA achieved more accurate acetabular component positioning and limb length restoration, but functional outcomes and overall complication rates showed no consistent superiority.
summary_en.validation: Evidence was synthesized from published clinical comparative studies with methodological quality and risk-of-bias appraisal.
